finding.title: Guard the force-unwrapped credential.user in FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl.createUserWithEmailAndPassword
finding.why: Every other credential.user access in this same file tolerates a null user (signInAndGetUser:74 and signInWithEmailLink:141 both route through _toAppUserOrNull). Here the `!` will throw a raw TypeError ('Null check operator used on a null value') instead of a typed, catchable error if Firebase ever returns a credential without a user — a TypeError carries no stable code (EH-5) and isn't a deliberately-thrown, meaningful exception, so it degrades straight to an opaque crash instead of a handleable condition, inconsistent with how the rest of the file treats the identical precondition.
finding.recommendation: Mirror the null-check-and-throw pattern used elsewhere in the file (or the typed exception recommended in the EH-5 finding) instead of force-unwrapping credential.user.
acceptance_criteria: No bare `!` on credential.user in this file.
A regression test exercises the null-user branch of createUserWithEmailAndPassword.

finding.title: Add inline // keepAlive: justification comments to auth_providers.dart's two singleton providers
finding.why: SM-6 requires every keepAlive: true to carry an inline `// keepAlive:` justification comment, specifically because the planned [Pending] audit grep keys off that literal tag beside the annotation (docs/coding-standards.md:156). Both providers here only have an ordinary doc comment above the function ('Provides the singleton ... used app-wide'), not the tagged comment the future checker looks for — when that grep ships, these two will false-positive as unjustified even though the reasoning is already documented in prose. (The same gap recurs at other keepAlive sites repo-wide, e.g. content_index.dart, registry_provider.dart, preference_providers.dart — those are outside this batch, noted here only for the orchestrator's dedup.)
finding.recommendation: Add a one-line `// keepAlive: <reason>` comment immediately above each @Riverpod(keepAlive: true), e.g. '// keepAlive: stateless singleton facade, cheap to keep for app lifetime'.
acceptance_criteria: Both providers carry a `// keepAlive:` tagged comment.
Future SM-6 audit grep (once shipped) passes for this file.

finding.title: Split firebase_auth_gateway_impl_test.dart — 496 lines exceeds the 400-line AG-3 ratchet
finding.why: AG-3's checker (`find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) explicitly scans test/ as well as lib/; this file is 496 lines, 96 over the ratchet. It is otherwise a well-structured, hermetic, mocktail-based suite with good branch coverage of the documented gateway contract — the size comes from covering ~20 gateway methods 1:1, not from disorganization.
finding.recommendation: Split by concern (e.g. an email/password test file, a Google-credential test file, a lifecycle/action-code test file) or extract the stubUser/mock-registration boilerplate into a shared test helper to shrink the file.
acceptance_criteria: `find learning_tracker/lib learning_tracker/test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` no longer lists this file or its replacements.

finding.title: content_grouping.dart groupItemsByNextLevel's maxBrowseDepth clamp silently reintroduces fixed bug R5-6
finding.rule: Evans (invariant re-derived, not enforced once) / doc-reality drift

evidence.quote: if (maxBrowseDepth != null && currentDepth >= maxBrowseDepth) return const [];

/// Pass [maxBrowseDepth] to stop at a particular depth (Browse Content caps at
/// `CurriculumLabels.maxBrowseDepth`).

// The old `>= maxBrowseDepth → return []` conflated "don't drill further"
// with "show nothing"; this fixes R5-6.

finding.why: docs/planning/bug-hunt-round5-findings-2026-05-31.md rates R5-6 'high': the browse tree showed 'No content' instead of the terminal chapter rows when a deep-link opened at max browse depth. That bug was fixed only in content_hierarchy_screen.dart's private, hand-duplicated `_groupItemsByNextLevel` (clamp to maxBrowseDepth-1, never return empty) — the fix was never ported back to the 'canonical' shared groupItemsByNextLevel this file exports, which still has the pre-fix `return const []` guard. Repo-wide grep confirms zero current callers pass maxBrowseDepth (Browse Content uses its own private copy instead, precisely because of this bug), so it's a dead branch today — but the doc comment explicitly invites a future caller to wire it up for exactly the Browse Content use case, which would resurrect the regression with zero warning.
finding.recommendation: Either delete content_hierarchy_screen.dart's private duplicate and make it call this shared function (after porting the maxBrowseDepth-1 clamp fix here), or fix the clamp here to match and correct the doc comment so it doesn't claim Browse Content already caps through this parameter.
acceptance_criteria: A test at test/core/content/content_grouping_test.dart calls groupItemsByNextLevel with currentDepth == maxBrowseDepth and asserts it returns the clamped terminal-level rows, not an empty list (regression for R5-6).
content_hierarchy_screen.dart no longer maintains a second, independently-fixed copy of this grouping logic.

finding.title: Convert HierarchySelection and AdjacentItems to @freezed instead of hand-rolled/missing equality
finding.rule: coding-standards.md:584 — never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes
finding.why: coding-standards.md is explicit: 'hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.' HierarchySelection is stored in `Set<HierarchySelection>` in production code (bulk_mark_screen.dart:68, hierarchy_selection_panel.dart:88) — Set.add/remove/contains rely directly on ==/hashCode. All 4 fields are covered today, but the next field added to the class (a plausible edit given it already models a 4-level hierarchy with headroom) will silently break selection dedup in the bulk-mark/lifetime-marking flows unless the two overrides are manually kept in sync. AdjacentItems has no equality at all (identity-only), so two structurally-equal instances never compare equal — currently harmless since it's only null-checked, but not an @freezed value type either.
finding.recommendation: Annotate both as @freezed (or add copyWith by hand and a comment justifying why not, matching the project's stated carve-out pattern) so equality/hashCode/copyWith stay generated and in sync with the fields.
acceptance_criteria: HierarchySelection and AdjacentItems are @freezed classes; all existing == /hashCode assertions in hierarchy_selection_test.dart and epic_25_schema_core_test.dart still pass unchanged.
Set<HierarchySelection> usage in bulk_mark_screen.dart and hierarchy_selection_panel.dart compiles and behaves identically.
